data.body:
S6 MERGED. Gerrit change 2609 ('Bound concurrent gate runs with fast-fail', commit a1e5a63aac11) reached LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 and was submitted; it is on main.

DESIGN AS LANDED. Admission takes the seam gate_peak_rss already documents -- wrapping review_plan()
and verify_completion() covers the MCP daemon path and the CLI at once -- but sits strictly OUTSIDE
it, enclosing resolve_gate_handle, because that is where the bytes are actually spent.

The counter is flock'd slot files in the snapshot store's EXISTING locks/ directory: cross-process,
and crash-safe WITHOUT a heartbeat because the kernel drops an flock when the holder dies. That
matters more than it sounds -- it delivers the property the PID+heartbeat lease was supposed to
provide, without reviving the design ADR 0112 records as rejected-as-unsound (N readers per entry,
PID reuse, crash-stale leases).

DEGRADATION SPLITS BY FAULT, which was the fifth plan-review block and the right one: a missing fcntl
or one bad slot file ADMITS AND ANNOUNCES, while an unreachable store root REFUSES
(GateScratchUnavailableError). Fail-open on an unreachable scratch volume would silently revert gate
bytes to the root filesystem -- which is the outage this epic exists to prevent, so failing open there
would have contradicted the ADR's own consequence.

DEFAULT CAP 4, derived rather than picked: 4 x ~748 MB is about 2.99 GB, which fits the ~3 GiB left
on the t4g.large after ~2.17 GB steady state and Gerrit's ~3 GiB reservation; a fifth concurrent run
at ~3.74 GB does not. Well below the ~10 concurrent observed in practice, which is the point.

FAST-FAIL, NOT QUEUE, per the operator's decision: at capacity the call returns a congestion error
naming the condition so the client can back off. Queueing was rejected because a queued gate still
holds the client's request open and MCP callers have a request deadline.

A REAL LATENT BUG WAS FOUND WHILE TESTING: _cli/_llm_commands._review_plan hardcoded 'return 1' for
an LLMError where its sibling calls _llm_error_exit_code. Caught by an AC test going RED at
'assert 1 == 11'.

Mutations, both restored: widening the slot scan to limit+1 turned 10 tests RED, including 'admitted
while another process held every slot' and both entry-point wiring tests; dropping the finally around
release_slot turned the slot-release-on-failure test RED with GateCongestedError on the follow-up
admission. That second one matters -- a cap that leaks slots on error degrades to a deadlock.

Verification: make lint exit 0 (complexity new=0 increased=0; mechanism new=0); make typecheck clean
(755 files); test_mechanism_delta.py 31 passed; targeted 32 passed; 2623-test regression sweep passed.

RECORDED DEVIATION: no REBAR_GATE_MAX_CONCURRENT env tier, unlike its neighbours. That was declined
citing the a1f1 mechanism-ratchet contradiction -- WHICH I LATER PROVED WAS FALSE. A correct
mechanism-ok marker does satisfy both ratchet tests. So the env tier can simply be added; it is a
small follow-up, not a blocked one. Not reopening this change for it, since 2609 is merged and the
tier is an ADR nicety rather than a correctness gap.

S6 was the PRECONDITION for S2-S5: the janitor reclaims by high-water mark over POSIX
delete-on-last-close, so bytes held by an in-flight gate are live rather than garbage, and a cap below
peak concurrent hold cannot be honoured by reclamation alone. With this landed, those stories are
unblocked.
